scenario_analysis.scenario: +2 C temperature diagnostics, -20% gridded mean precipitation, +15% peak wind, +10% exposed population

mechanism_chain: High burn-change metrics indicate a strong fire source in the event area.
The available daily weather records are mostly dry, hot, and windy enough to support sustained fire spread and smoke production, with coverage tracked separately.
Report text explicitly links wildfire emissions, transport, air quality, PM2.5, and health-relevant exposure using once-per-term presence scoring.
Population, critical facilities, and nearby Brazil wildfire catalog points make the smoke episode operationally consequential.
primary_gt.final_interpretation: The coupled model classifies the episode as extreme at baseline and remains extreme under the hotter, drier, windier, higher-exposure scenario, with a material stress increase.

event.event_name: 2024 South America historic wildfire smoke emissions
event.hazard_label: Air pollution, smoke, and heat exposure
event.location: Amazon and Pantanal, Bolivia and Brazil

event_window.coverage_note: Daily weather calculations use only available package records inside the event window.

transport_exposure.term_count_rule: Each process term is counted once if present at least once in the selected report corpus or locked event-anchor notes after lowercasing; repeated occurrences are not counted.

criteria.name: Self-directed package discovery and citations
criteria.description: Finds relevant package files independently and cites package-relative paths spanning reports, hazard products, remote sensing, exposure, geospatial context, and catalogs.
criteria.partial_credit: Award up to 2 points for incomplete but useful multi-family citations.

criteria.name: Event window, weather coverage, and AOI geometry
criteria.description: Correctly derives the 52-day inclusive event window, 46 available weather-record days, coverage fraction, and approximate AOI area from the polygon without inferring missing daily weather values.
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1 point for each correct group of calculations.

criteria.name: Source severity and remote-sensing calculations
criteria.description: Correctly extracts dNBR mean/max, annual embedding change mean/max, computes the peak-to-mean ratios, and applies the source component formula.
criteria.partial_credit: Award proportional credit for correct extraction and formula use.

criteria.name: Hot-dry-wind process component
criteria.description: Correctly computes the three temperature diagnostics, dry-day fraction, wind unit conversion, precipitation suppression, and the combined hot-dry-wind component.
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for each correct subterm within tolerance.

criteria.name: Transport and exposure component
criteria.description: Correctly detects the six process terms using once-per-term presence scoring, computes person-day exposure, counts critical facilities, finds the nearest Brazil wildfire catalog point, and combines the component.
criteria.partial_credit: Award proportional credit for correct text, exposure, facility, and catalog subterms.

criteria.name: Baseline and scenario stress model
criteria.description: Correctly computes baseline index/class and the warmer-drier-windier-higher-exposure scenario index, delta, class, and worsening flag.
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for a correct baseline or scenario with minor rounding errors.

criteria.name: Disaster-process interpretation and valid JSON
criteria.description: Returns parseable JSON with a concise mechanism chain and interpretation grounded in wildfire source, weather, transport, and exposure evidence.
criteria.partial_credit: No credit for generic explanation not tied to the computed model.

provenance.notes: All values are recomputed from local CSX-207 package files; no network access is used. Daily weather metrics use available records through the package record end and weather_coverage_fraction records partial event coverage.
